newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS PREPARE FOR FINAL PUSH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS PREPARE FOR FINAL PUSH.

text.p: A season which began back in February will finally end for South Africa on Sunday when the battle-weary Springboks face Wales in a one-off test at Cardiff Arms Park.

It has been, to put it mildly, a long, tough season which on a provincial level began with the innovative, spell-binding rugby of the Super 12 and continued with an expanded domestic Currie Cup competition.
At the heart of it, though, has been the expanding international calender. Sunday's test will be the Springboks' 13th of the year, including four defeats to New Zealand and one to Australia.
It is a programme which has seen most of the side in Cardiff play upwards of 40 matches this season, with some appearing in more than 50, but the South Africans are unlikely to lie down quietly.
Their recent 2-0 series win over the French was a result of hard, attritional rugby, and coach Andre Markgraaff is making no apologies.

"Maybe for the spectators that's not attractive but we want to win and we play to win," he says. "We have had enough pressure this season and now we must just win. We have a mission on this tour and we must complete that mission."

Markgraaff knows all about pressure. Appointed as replacement to World Cup winning coach Kitch Christie at the start of the season he came under fire after presiding over the Springboks' first home series defeat by the All Blacks.
When he axed the hugely popular captain Francois Pienaar from the current tour party he faced a barrage of death threats and hate mail, but he now sees some light at the end of the tunnel.

"What we have achieved in Argentina and France is some consistency. We have had the same side for five tests running and that means a side which is settling. Trust me, you won't see the best of this team until next year when the British Lions come out to South Africa."

Welsh captain Johnathan Humphreys has spoken about matching the Springboks physically and memories will doubtless float back to Ellis Park last year when lock Kobus Wiese knocked out his opposite number Derwyn Jones.

Wiese was fined heavily at the time but is now a key member of the Springbok pack. Jones, however, is missing, dropped after an anonymous performance in this month's 29-18 defeat by Australia, and replaced by the 32-year-old Mark Rowley.

The Welsh looked slow and short of ideas in that game and will be keen for an improved performance against South Africa, a side they have never beaten in their previous nine encounters dating back to 1906.

A mouth injury has ruled out centre Gareth Thomas and his place goes to Alan Bateman, capped for the first time since his return from rugby league. His elevation ensures an all-league midfield alongside Scott Gibbs and fly-half Johnathan Davies.

Wales - 15-Neil Jenkins; 14-Ieuan Evans, 13-Scott Gibbs, 12-Allen Bateman, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Jonathan Davies, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Steve Williams, 7-Colin Charvis, 6-Dale McIntosh, 5-Mark Rowley, 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-David Young, 2-Jonathan Humphreys (captain), 1-Christian Loader.

South Africa - 15-Andre Joubert; 14-James Small, 13-Japie Mulder, 12-Hennie le Roux, 11-Jacques Olivier; 10-Henry Honiball, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen; 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Kobus Wiese, 3-Adrian Garvey, 2-James Dalton, 1-Dawie Theron.
